summary: Full backend test of new rate-limiter (login 5/900s, forgot 3/3600s, signup 10/3600s) and /api/billing/payments history endpoint. All 12 new tests pass + 66 regression tests (23 plan_limits + 26 auth_ext + 17 billing) = 78/78 backend tests passing. Verified: login 5-fail→401 then 6th→429 with Retry-After; login success resets bucket; forgot 3 OK then 4th 429; signup 10 OK then 11th 429; X-Forwarded-For gives independent buckets; failed Razorpay create-order does NOT insert into db.payments; manually-inserted payment record returned with plan_name/amount_inr derived and razorpay_signature + _id EXCLUDED; multi-record history sorted desc by created_at.

POST /api/auth/login: 6th failure returns 429 with Retry-After header (integer seconds, 0<n<=905)
POST /api/auth/login: after 4 fails + 1 success, counter resets — next 5 fails still 401, 6th is 429

critical_code_review_comments: rate_limit.py: uses global module-level _store dict guarded by a single threading.Lock. Fine for single-worker uvicorn but will diverge across workers/pods — swap for Redis before horizontal scaling. Comment in the file already flags this.

rate_limit._client_ip trusts X-Forwarded-For blindly (takes the first hop). At the edge (ingress) this is correct only if the ingress overwrites/appends XFF. If a client attaches their own XFF header and the ingress appends rather than replaces, an attacker could rotate the leftmost value to bypass rate limiting. Recommendation: use the LAST value in XFF as set by ingress, or use a trusted-proxy list.

billing.build_router.payments_history: uses projection {'_id': 0, 'razorpay_signature': 0} — correctly hides signature. Sort is DESC on created_at (ISO strings) which relies on lexicographic sort of same-tz ISO. Safe as long as all created_at have the same +00:00 suffix (verified). Limit is to_list(200) — no pagination; add cursor/page if user could accumulate >200 payments.
billing.build_router.payments_history: plan_name lookup falls back to plan_id string if the plan id is unknown — good defensive default. Note amount_inr rounds to 2 decimals from paise; correct.

server.py login: reset_bucket is only called after a *successful* verify_password. Correct — brute-forcers do not benefit. However, reset_bucket runs after every successful login so a valid user occasionally hitting wrong-then-right does not accumulate. Good.
server.py signup: rate limit is 10/hr per IP but there is no throttling on Razorpay create-order or on chat endpoints. If cost-sensitive endpoints are added later, apply the same pattern.
auth_ext.forgot_password: check_rate raises 429 BEFORE the DB lookup so it does not leak whether the email exists via timing. Good.
No tests for concurrent (thread) requests against rate limiter; the deque + Lock code is straightforward but a stress test would be worth adding under a mocked clock.
Retry-After header uses integer seconds computed as (window - (now - q[0])) + 1; can be as low as 1s if the oldest hit is about to age out. Acceptable behavior.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/conftest.py (created) — installs a per-test-file X-Forwarded-For header so pre-existing test files (which never sent XFF) don't share the rate-limit bucket with the new tests and get their own isolated bucket. Existing tests unaware of rate limiting continue to pass; new tests that explicitly set XFF are respected.
test_credentials: Fresh isolated users per test class: rt-<slug>-<hex>@test.com / pass1234. Cleaned up in session teardown via _db.users.delete_many({'email': {'$regex': '^rt-'}}).
seed_data_creation: 12+ ephemeral users created via signup. 4 db.payments rows inserted directly via pymongo for the billing-history record test and multi-record ordering test — all cleaned up in test finally blocks. Rate limiter is in-memory; backend restarted once before the full run to guarantee a clean state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rate limiter is process-local. If you run the whole test dir, /app/backend/tests/conftest.py auto-injects a unique X-Forwarded-For per test file so buckets don't collide. If you add tests that hit /auth/login, /auth/signup, or /auth/forgot-password, either rely on the conftest OR set your own X-Forwarded-For (see TestLoginRateLimit.XFF pattern using unique third-octet). To reset all buckets, `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. MongoDB access: MONGO_URL + DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env, collections used: db.payments (fields: id, user_id, plan_id, razorpay_order_id, razorpay_payment_id, razorpay_signature, amount, currency, status, created_at, paid_at). /api/billing/payments returns amount_inr = round(amount/100, 2) and plan_name from PLANS[plan_id].name. Response projection strips _id and razorpay_signature.
rca of the issue: N/A — no failures. All rate-limit and billing-history behaviour matches spec. A transient regression appeared during the very first full-suite run because pre-existing tests share the same client IP with the new rate-limit tests (the runners have no ingress that appends XFF, so all requests without XFF hash to a single (client.host, bucket) key). The conftest.py XFF-injection fix isolates each test file's bucket and the full suite passes cleanly.
